arxiv-1912-01546.title: On the deficiency of complete multipartite graphs
arxiv-1912-01546.creator: A.R. Davtyan, G.M. Minasyan[MCSD], P.A. Petrosyan[MCSD]
arxiv-1912-01546.description: Abstract An edge-coloring of a graph G G with colors 1 , … , t 1,\ldots,t is an interval t t -coloring if all colors are used, and the colors of edges incident to each vertex of G G are distinct and form an integer interval. It is well-known that there are graphs that do not have interval colorings.

arxiv-2004-13513.title: PODNet: Pooled Outputs Distillation for Small-Tasks Incremental Learning
arxiv-2004-13513.creator: Arthur Douillard, Matthieu Cord, Charles Ollion, Thomas Robert, Eduardo Valle
arxiv-2004-13513.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Arthur Douillard, Matthieu Cord, Charles Ollion, Thomas Robert, Eduardo Valle. Lifelong learning has attracted much attention, but existing works still struggle to fight catastrophic forgetting and accumulate knowledge over long stretches of incremental learning. In this work, we propose PODNet, a model inspired by representation learning. By carefully balancing the compromise between remembering the old classes and learning new ones, PODNet fights catastrophic forgetting, even over very long runs of small incremental tasks -- a setting so far unexplored by current works.

arxiv-2011-06610.title: The Swampland at Large Number of Space-Time Dimensions Preprint: LMU-ASC 40/20 Preprint: MPP-2020-192 Preprint: DESY 20-185
arxiv-2011-06610.creator: Quentin Bonnefoy, Luca Ciambelli, Dieter Lüst, Severin Lüst
arxiv-2011-06610.description: Abstract We discuss some aspects of swampland constraints - especially the swampland distance conjecture - in a large number of space-time dimensions D D . We analyze Kaluza-Klein (KK) states at large D D and find that some KK spectra possess an interesting dependence on D D .

arxiv-2011-07082.title: ELT Imaging of MWC 297 from the 23-m LBTI: Complex Disk Structure and a Companion Candidate
arxiv-2011-07082.creator: S. Sallum, J.A. Eisner, J.M. Stone, J. Dietrich, P. Hinz, E. Spalding
arxiv-2011-07082.description: Abstract Herbig Ae / Be stars represent the early outcomes of star formation and the initial stages of planet formation at intermediate stellar masses. Understanding both of these processes requires detailed characterization of their disk structures and companion frequencies. We present new 3.

arxiv-2205-06457.title: ViT5: Pretrained Text-to-Text Transformer for Vietnamese Language Generation
arxiv-2205-06457.creator: Long Phan 1,2 , Hieu Tran 1 , Hieu Nguyen 1,2 , Trieu H. Trinh 1,3 1 VietAI Research 2 Case Western Reserve University 3 New York University long.phan@case.edu
arxiv-2205-06457.description: Abstract We present ViT5, a pretrained Transformer-based encoder-decoder model for the Vietnamese language. With T5-style self-supervised pretraining, ViT5 is trained on a large corpus of high-quality and diverse Vietnamese texts. We benchmark ViT5 on two downstream text generation tasks, Abstractive Text Summarization and Named Entity Recognition.

arxiv-2303-03930.title: Nonlinear optics from hybrid dispersive orbits
arxiv-2303-03930.creator: Yongjun Li ID, Derong Xu, Victor Smaluk, Robert Rainer ID
arxiv-2303-03930.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yongjun Li ID, Derong Xu, Victor Smaluk, Robert Rainer ID. In this paper we present an expansion of the technique of characterizing nonlinear optics from off-energy orbits (NOECO) Olsson et al. 2020 to cover harmonic sextupoles in storage rings. The existing NOECO technique has been successfully used to correct the chromatic sextupole errors on the MAX-IV machine, however, it doesn’t account for harmonic sextupoles, which are widely used on many other machines.

arxiv-2311-04439.title: A Geometric Extension of the Itô-Wentzell and Kunita’s Formulas
arxiv-2311-04439.creator: Aythami Bethencourt de León 1, 2, ∗, So Takao 1, 3
arxiv-2311-04439.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Aythami Bethencourt de León 1, 2, ∗, So Takao 1, 3. We extend the Itô-Wentzell formula for the evolution along a continuous semimartingale of a time-dependent stochastic field driven by a continuous semimartingale to tensor field-valued stochastic processes on manifolds. More concretely, we investigate how the pull-back (respectively, the push-forward) by a stochastic flow of diffeomorphisms of a time-dependent stochastic tensor field driven by a continuous semimartingale evolves with time, deriving it under suitable regularity conditions.

arxiv-2404-17423.title: Forming off-center massive black hole binaries in dwarf galaxies through Jacobi capture
arxiv-2404-17423.creator: Thibaut L. François ,, Christian M. Boily, Jonathan Freundlich, Simon Rozier, Karina Voggel
arxiv-2404-17423.description: Abstract It is well established that black holes reside in the central regions of virtually all types of known galaxies. Recent observational and numerical studies however challenge this picture, suggesting that intermediate-mass black holes in dwarf galaxies may be found on orbits far from the center.

arxiv-2405-08884.title: Finite-element assembly approach of optical quantum walk networks
arxiv-2405-08884.creator: Christopher R. Schwarze, 1, * David S. Simon, 1,2, Anthony D. Manni, 1 Abdoulaye Ndao, 1,3 and Alexander V. Sergienko 1,4
arxiv-2405-08884.description: Abstract We present a finite-element approach for computing the aggregate scattering matrix of a network of linear coherent scatterers. These might be optical scatterers or more general scattering coins studied in quantum walk theory. While techniques exist for two-dimensional lattices of feed-forward scatterers, the present approach is applicable to any network configuration of any collection of scatterers.

arxiv-2411-07161.title: RoundTable: Investigating Group Decision-Making Mechanism in Multi-Agent Collaboration
arxiv-2411-07161.creator: Young-Min Cho, Raphael Shu, Nilaksh Das, Tamer Alkhouli, Yi-An Lai, Jason Cai, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang, Dan Roth
arxiv-2411-07161.description: Abstract Effective group decision-making is critical in Multi-Agent Systems (MAS). Yet, how different mechanisms for reaching consensus impact collaboration quality and efficiency remains understudied. We conduct a systematic study on group decision-making mechanisms in a decentralized setting. Through controlled experiments, we analyze how different voting rules affect decision quality and efficiency in a multi-round collaboration.

arxiv-2508-02925.title: Goal-Oriented Adaptive Finite Element Multilevel Quasi-Monte Carlo
arxiv-2508-02925.creator: Joakim Beck, Yang Liu, Erik von Schwerin, Raúl Tempone
arxiv-2508-02925.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joakim Beck, Yang Liu, Erik von Schwerin, Raúl Tempone. The efficient approximation of quantity of interest derived from PDEs with lognormal diffusivity is a central challenge in uncertainty quantification. In this study, we propose a multilevel quasi-Monte Carlo framework to approximate deterministic, real-valued, bounded linear functionals that depend on the solution of a linear elliptic PDE with a lognormal diffusivity coefficient parameterized by a 49-dimensional Gaussian random vector and deterministic geometric singularities in bounded domains of ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} .

arxiv-2511-03564.description: Abstract The ENDF/B-VIII.1 library is the newest recommended evaluated nuclear data file by the Cross Section Evaluation Working Group (CSEWG) for use in nuclear science and technology applications, and incorporates advances made in the six years since the release of ENDF/B-VIII.0.

pmc-10574971.title: Grant-Free NOMA: A Low-Complexity Power Control through User Clustering
pmc-10574971.creator: Abdulkadir Celik
pmc-10574971.description: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has emerged as a promising solution to support multiple devices on the same network resources, improving spectral efficiency and enabling massive connectivity required by ever-increasing Internet of Things devices. However, traditional NOMA schemes operate in a grant-based fashion and require channel-state information and power control, which hinders its implementation for massive machine-type communications.

pmc-10593824.title: Reproducibility of APT-weighted CEST-MRI at 3T in healthy brain and tumor across sessions and scanners
pmc-10593824.creator: Yulun Wu, Tobias C Wood, Sophie H A E Derks, Ilanah J Pruis, Sebastian van der Voort, Sophie E M Veldhuijzen van Zanten, Marion Smits, Esther A H Warnert
pmc-10593824.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Amide proton transfer (APT)-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) imaging is a recent MRI technique making its way into clinical application. In this work, we investigated whether APT-weighted CEST imaging can provide reproducible measurements across scan sessions and scanners. Within-session, between-session and between scanner reproducibility was calculated for 19 healthy volunteers and 7 patients with a brain tumor on two 3T MRI scanners.

pmc-10686665.title: Incidental Adrenal Masses: A Case Report of an Adrenal Oncocytoma
pmc-10686665.creator: Bruno Giesteira, Jessica Sousa, João Pinheiro Amorim
pmc-10686665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). A 59-year-old woman underwent an abdominal and pelvic computed tomography (CT) scan to rule out non-obstructive urolithiasis. The patient was asymptomatic, with the exception of occasional bilateral low back pain. A physical examination did not reveal any notable findings.The CT scan revealed the presence of an incidental solid left adrenal lesion, which displaced the body of the pancreas and the left kidney. The lesion measured 7 cm × 6.5 cm and exhibited a rounded morphology with well-defined margins.

pmc-11348926.title: Long-Term Observation of Prognostic Factors and Clinical Outcome of Vernal Keratoconjunctivitis in Childhood
pmc-11348926.creator: Asami Shimokawa, Aya Ikeda, Kazuhiro Harada, Rie Takahashi, Jane Huang, Tomoko Tsukahara-Kawamura, Hiroaki Ozaki, Eiichi Uchio
pmc-11348926.description: PurposeVernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC) is a refractory ocular allergic disorder that mainly affects boys. Long-term follow-up has been rarely reported for VKC. We investigated the long-term clinical outcome of VKC to identify relevant clinical features of prognostic value based on follow-up for a median of 70 months.

pmc-11564157.title: Nomogram model based on clinical factors and autonomic nervous system activity for predicting residual renal function decline in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis
pmc-11564157.creator: Jing Wang, Zhenye Chen, Yaoyu Huang, Yujun Qian, Hongqing Cui, Li Zhang, Yike Zhang, Ningning Wang, Hongwu Chen, Haibin Ren, Huijuan Mao
pmc-11564157.description: BackgroundSeveral heart rate variability (HRV) parameters were reported to be associated with residual renal function (RRF) in patients undergoing continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD). However, it is unclear whether using HRV or other autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity indexes can predict RRF decline in CAPD patients.

pmc-11692306.title: PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND EXERCISE-INDUCED NEUROTROPHIC AND CORTISOL RESPONSES: PRELIMINARY RESULTS
pmc-11692306.creator: Thinh Huynh, Baylie Rushing, Madeleine Love, Denise Head, Marta Stojanovic
pmc-11692306.description: Neurotrophic and cortisol responses to a bout of exercise are a pathway for understanding the potential mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of regular physical activity on cognitive and brain health. However, there is limited understanding of the factors that moderate such responses.

pmc-11859583.title: Variables Predicting Psychological Help Seeking Attitudes: Self-Stigma, Mental Health Literacy, and Depression/Anxiety
pmc-11859583.creator: H. Gündoğdu, K. Aslan, H. C. Ayhan, C. M. Aktaş
pmc-11859583.description: Introduction Psychological help-seeking attitudes are influenced by various factors, including self-stigma, mental health literacy, and levels of depression and anxiety. Several studies have examined the relationships between these variables and help-seeking attitudes, shedding light on the predictors of seeking psychological help. Self-stigma, or the internalization of negative attitudes towards seeking psychological help, has been found to significantly impact help-seeking attitudes.

pmc-12436200.title: What Influences Maternal Stress in The NICU Among Mothers of Preterm Infants?
pmc-12436200.creator: Halyna Pavlyshyn, Iryna Sarapuk
pmc-12436200.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). PurposeTo assess the levels of stress and anxiety in mothers of preterm infants across various gestational ages (GA) and identify GA-specific factors contributing to maternal stress.Patients and MethodsStress and worry were measured in 146 mothers of infants ≤32 weeks GA and 101 mothers >32 weeks GA using the Parental Stressor Scale: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (PSS: NICU) and Worry Index (WI) questionnaires.

pmc-12580303.title: A concise guide to fluorescent cell cycle reporters for live-cell imaging
pmc-12580303.creator: Jinyu Wang, Yige Li, Jia Luo, Septavera Sharvia, Kuan Yoow Chan
pmc-12580303.description: The cell cycle is a fundamental process vital for organismal growth and stability. Its dysregulation underlies many human diseases, in particular cancers, making its monitoring essential in biological research. Genetically encoded fluorescent cell cycle reporters have become indispensable tools for studying the cell cycle, providing invaluable insights into cell cycle dynamics at single-cell resolution.

pmc-12653269.title: Breast-Conserving Surgery in BRCA Mutation Carriers: A Paradigm Shift Toward Individualized, Multidisciplinary Care
pmc-12653269.creator: Calogero Cipolla, Giuseppa Scandurra, Daniela Sambataro, Chiara Mesi, Martina Greco, Eleonora D’Agati, Vittorio Gebbia, Luca Giacomelli, Maria Rosaria Valerio, Alejandro Martin Sanchez, Angela Bucaro, Flavia de Lauretis
pmc-12653269.description: Breast cancer associated with BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations presents unique therapeutic challenges, traditionally favoring mastectomy due to concerns over recurrence and new primaries. However, evolving evidence and advances in multimodal therapy have reshaped this paradigm, positioning breast-conserving surgery (BCS) as a viable option for selected carriers.

pmc-12669772.title: Mechanism of autophagy initiation by transmembrane selective autophagy receptors
pmc-12669772.creator: Elias Adriaenssens, Sascha Martens
pmc-12669772.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Selective autophagy ensures the targeted degradation of damaged or surplus cellular components, including organelles, thereby safeguarding cellular homeostasis. This process relies on selective autophagy receptors (SARs) that link specific cargo to the autophagy machinery. These receptors exist in two distinct forms: soluble SARs that are recruited to the cargo on demand, and transmembrane SARs that are stably embedded in the membranes of organelles they target.

pmc-13013525.title: The tumor microenvironment shapes gastric cancer progression by coordinating immune suppression and metabolic reprogramming
pmc-13013525.creator: Fuzhi Jiao, Zhen Wang, Jing Yuan, Fenglei Shi, Shengnan Zhang
pmc-13013525.description: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, largely owing to metastasis driven by a highly dynamic tumor microenvironment (TME). Immunosuppressive regulatory T cells (Tregs) and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) orchestrate immune evasion through checkpoint signaling and polarization programs, while cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) reshape stromal architecture and promote hypoxia.

pmc-13205384.title: Dental Glass Ionomer Cement for Root Perforation Management: Physicochemical Characteristics and In Vitro Cell Response
pmc-13205384.creator: Alexandra Popa, Radu-Vasile Radulescu, Florentina Rus, Vlad Gabriel Vasilescu, Lucian Toma Ciocan, Monica Musteanu, Marina Imre, Silviu Pituru, Ana Cernega, Alexandra Ripszky, Ecaterina Andronescu
pmc-13205384.description: Background/Objectives: Root perforation treatment is essential for restoring the tightness of the root system, preventing periradicular inflammation and tooth loss. pmc-13459783.creator: Beverly Egyir, Alex Awentirim Akayiri, Emmanuel Ohene Kyei McKeown, Daniel Kwaku Baka, William Boateng, Christian Owusu-Nyantakyi, Grebstad Rabbi Amuasi, Quaneeta Mohktar, Gabriella Acquah, Maa Lankai Quaye, Alfred Bortey, Emmanuel Gberbi, Angella Yayra Kampo, Agnes Oclu, Justice Danso, Blessing Kof

ANNOUNCEMENT Wastewater surveillance combined with whole-genome sequencing enables high-resolution monitoring of antimicrobial resistance and supports public health responses (1–7).

pmc-13487289.title: The relationship between congenital infections and autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review
pmc-13487289.creator: Alice W Jung, Júlia Supptitz, Pedro Nunes Hummes, Rafaela Jung Kurtz Rodrigues, Magda Lahorgue Nunes
pmc-13487289.description: ObjectiveThe aim of this systematic review (SR) is to evaluate the relationship between congenital infections (Toxoplasmosis, Cytomegalovirus, Rubella, Herpes simplex type 1 and 2, HIV, Zika, and Syphilis) and the development of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).Data sourceThe authors seek to identify loopholes in the current knowledge about this content and to understand the role of congenital infections in children’s neurodevelopment.
